questions.question: Q: What is the advantage of watching a live performance over a recorded one?

points.text: Live performance provides the full sensory experience — you feel the energy, scale and atmosphere in real time, and the audience-performer relationship is immediate and tangible.

questions.question: Q: Why is repeated viewing useful when analysing a recorded dance?

points.text: Repeated viewing lets you focus on different elements each time — first the overall structure, then specific movement details, design features or dancer relationships.

questions.question: Q: How do the four content categories help structure an analysis?

points.text: They provide a systematic framework so you cover all aspects: action (what), dynamics (how), space (where) and relationships (who), ensuring nothing is missed.

questions.question: Q: Why should analysis always reference the choreographic intention?

points.text: Every choreographic choice serves the intention — linking your analysis to it shows you understand why decisions were made, not just what they are.

questions.question: Q: Name two design elements you should consider alongside movement when analysing a dance.

points.text: Costume and lighting — though set/staging and aural setting are also valid design elements that contribute to meaning.
